description:
Location: crate-jmap-base-client/src/auth.rs (BearerAuth, BasicAuth, ClientError)

BACKGROUND
BearerAuth (auth.rs:183-189) and BasicAuth (auth.rs:233-239) both have
manually-written Debug impls that redact their credential fields:
  f.debug_struct("BearerAuth").field("token", &"[REDACTED]").finish()
  f.debug_struct("BasicAuth").field("credentials", &"[REDACTED]").finish()

This is the correct hygiene. The AuthProvider trait doc-comment (auth.rs:100-101)
also instructs:
  /// Implementations **must not** log the return value of [`auth_header`];
  /// it contains credentials.

CONCERN
None of these invariants are enforced by a test. A maintainer who later
adds #[derive(Debug)] to BearerAuth (clearing the manual impl), or who
adds a new AuthProvider impl that prints its credentials in Debug, will
break the hygiene silently. The only thing catching that today would be
a manual code review.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a regression test under crate-jmap-base-client/src/auth.rs (or in
the existing #[cfg(test)] mod) that:

1. Constructs a BearerAuth with a known, distinctive token literal
   (e.g. 'CANARY-TOKEN-DO-NOT-LEAK-123').
2. Calls {:?}.format on the BearerAuth and asserts the literal
   substring 'CANARY-TOKEN-DO-NOT-LEAK-123' does NOT appear in the
   output.
3. Same for BasicAuth with a canary password.
4. Same for the auth_header()-returning AuthProvider trait object —
   formatted with {:?} (via Box<dyn AuthProvider>).

A few-line test that nails the contract. The cost is trivial; the
benefit is that any future refactor that exposes credentials via Debug
fails CI immediately rather than silently leaking into a docker-log
shipping pipeline somewhere downstream.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P3 (hygiene / defense-in-depth). Today's code is correct. This is a
tripwire against future regressions, in the same spirit as the existing
consecutive_skip_cap_matches_documented_value test in ws/mod.rs.

ORACLE
The canary string is the independent oracle — it is a literal under the
test's control, not derived from BearerAuth's internal state. The
assertion checks a property (absence of substring) rather than a value
derived from the code under test.
title: Security: workspace lacks a regression test asserting Authorization tokens never appear in Debug/Display output
